info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package tools is everything your org can call, in one list: connector actions, functions, agents, skills and your own MCP servers.

get.summary: Lists every tool the caller's org and project can reach, from every source, each flagged with whether it is activated.
get.description:
Lists every tool the caller's org and project can reach, from every
source, each flagged with whether it is activated. This is the discovery
surface: one flat set of names spanning connector actions, user functions,
zap-service routes, agents, skills and the org's own external MCP servers,
deduplicated by name so the highest-precedence source wins a collision. It
lists; it does not call — dispatch is POST /v1/tool/call.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description:
Source keeps only tools from one source — connector, function, zap-service,
agent, skill or mcp. Empty keeps every source.

parameters.name: activated
parameters.description:
Activated keeps only the tools activated for the caller's org and project,
and only when it is exactly the string "true".

get.summary: Reports which tools are switched on for the caller's org and project.
get.description:
Reports which tools are switched on for the caller's org and
project. Activation is what makes a tool dispatchable and what makes it visible
to an agent, so this is the set the MCP tool list is drawn from — every other
tool in the registry is discoverable but refused at call time.

put.summary: Switches tools on and off for the caller's org and project, and answers with the resulting activated set.
put.description:
Switches tools on and off for the caller's org and project, and
answers with the resulting activated set. It is the ONE write path that turns
skills, plugins and connectors into callable tools — an unactivated tool is
listed by discovery but refused 403 at dispatch. Activate is applied before
Deactivate, so a name in both lists ends up off. More than 256 toggles in one
request is refused 413.

Switching a skill (skill_<name>) or a tool of an MCP server the org registered
(<server>_<tool>) changes what every agent run in the org carries, so it takes
an admin of the org or a SuperAdmin: a member naming one is refused 403 and
nothing in the request is switched. Every change is on the org's audit trail
before it is made, and one the trail cannot record is refused 503.

post.summary: Runs one of the caller's activated tools and answers with its output.
post.description:
Runs one of the caller's activated tools and answers with its output.

This is the endpoint onto the tool plane's DYNAMIC half — the half no build-time
catalogue can hold, because it is per-tenant: an org's connected connector
actions, its authored skills, its agents and functions, and the tools of every
external MCP server it registered. A tool's existence, its price and its
activation are all rows, not code, so they cannot be known until the caller is.

One policy, the registry's: resolve by precedence, refuse an unactivated tool
403, settle a priced one through the x402 client or fail closed 402, then
dispatch to the winning source bound to the caller's own (org, project). One
metered unit, one audit record. A caller can only ever dispatch its own tools.

Discovery is GET /v1/tool — ?activated=true for the callable set.

get.summary: Lists the MCP servers the public registries publish, as we hold them: our canonical copy of registry.modelcontextprotocol.io, plus what we decided about each entry.
get.description:
Lists the MCP servers the public registries publish, as we hold
them: our canonical copy of registry.modelcontextprotocol.io, plus what we
decided about each entry.

This is the SHELF an org picks from. A listing with a streamable-http endpoint
can be enabled as-is — POST /v1/tool/mcp/servers with its id — and its tools then
join the org's tool plane and the fleet's MCP server. A listing that only ships a
stdio package needs a process to run it, which is why the transports are on
every entry rather than implied.

Hidden entries are absent: they are the ones we took off the shelf. A platform
SuperAdmin sees them, because the same query answers "what is on the shelf" and
"what is in the catalog" and two queries would drift apart.

It is PAGED — 50 by default, 200 at most. The public registry publishes tens of
thousands of servers, so an unbounded answer is a twenty-megabyte response and a
storefront that renders in a minute. total is the whole match, not the page.

It needs no credential: the shelf is a copy of public registries, the same for
every org, and a storefront shows it to a visitor before anyone signs in.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Q matches the name, title or description, case-insensitively.

parameters.name: featured
parameters.description:
Featured keeps only the listings we put on the front of the shelf, and only
when it is exactly the string "true".

parameters.name: official
parameters.description:
Official keeps only the vendors' OWN servers — not third-party copies of
them — and only when it is exactly the string "true".

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Limit bounds the page: default 50, maximum 200. A value that is not a
positive integer reads as the default.

post.summary: Pulls the public MCP registry into our canonical copy and reports what changed.
post.description:
Pulls the public MCP registry into our canonical copy and reports
what changed. SuperAdmin only; every other caller is refused.

It is IDEMPOTENT: a listing is keyed by the publisher's own reverse-DNS name,
so a second pass over an unchanged registry rewrites the same rows and reports
added=0, updated=0. It never deletes — a listing that vanishes upstream may be
one an org has already enabled, and dropping its description would not drop its
server. And it never touches CURATION: hidden, featured, an admin-set official
and a logo survive every sync, because the write does not name those columns.

get.summary: Returns one catalog entry in full: the publisher's description, its repository and site, every package form with the runtime that launches it, and every hosted endpoint.
get.description:
Returns one catalog entry in full: the publisher's description, its
repository and site, every package form with the runtime that launches it, and
every hosted endpoint. It is what a branding page renders, and what tells a
caller whether the listing can be enabled here and now (a streamable-http
remote) or needs somewhere to run first (a stdio package).

A HIDDEN listing is not served to an org — a shelf that renders what it does
not list would be a way around the shelf — but is served to a SuperAdmin, who
is the one deciding whether to put it back. Like the shelf, it needs no
credential.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
ID is the listing, from the path. It is the publisher's reverse-DNS name
with its one slash written as an underscore — "com.stripe_mcp".

patch.summary: Sets what WE say about one catalog entry — hidden, featured, official, logo — and answers with the stored listing.
patch.description:
Sets what WE say about one catalog entry — hidden, featured,
official, logo — and answers with the stored listing. SuperAdmin only; every
other caller is refused.

Curation is the half of a catalog row a sync cannot write, and this is the only
thing that writes it. The upstream half is never editable here: a description
that disagreed with the publisher's would be a fork of their listing, and the
next sync would silently undo it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the listing to curate, from the path.

post.summary: Recommends which skills and tools in the caller's org and project fit a prompt, and optionally activates them automatically.
post.description:
Recommends which skills and tools in the caller's org and project fit a
prompt, and optionally activates them automatically.

Every candidate is ranked by what its name and description say against the
prompt, the rarer a shared word the more it counts, through one vocabulary
for how people ask ("phones" and "responsive", "excel" and "xlsx"). Its
probability needs enough of that evidence, and a candidate well behind the
best of its kind (a skill, or an operation or tool) is held under 0.8, so a
prompt no skill fits recommends none. When autoActivate is true, recommended
entries that are not yet enabled — and that the caller has authority to
toggle — are activated in the caller's (org, project) scope and recorded on
the audit trail.

example.prompt: Review this React pull request and fix the responsive layout bug

get.summary: Answers the caller's kit: what their coding runs carry of the org's tool plane.
get.description:
Answers the caller's kit: what their coding runs carry of the org's tool
plane. Skills are the documents of those an admin of the org activated; servers
are those an admin registered, each by its id with the tools of it an admin
activated — never an address or a credential, which stay on the plane. Both
leave out what the caller muted, and muted names it. It is the one read a run
makes, so what it answers is what the caller's runs carry.

put.summary: Mutes and unmutes names of the org's kit for the caller's own runs, and answers the caller's kit after.
put.description:
Mutes and unmutes names of the org's kit for the caller's own runs, and
answers the caller's kit after. The layer only narrows: a name the org's kit
does not carry is refused 400, since muting it would say nothing, and unmuting
never gives the caller more than an admin put in place. It is the caller's own,
so any member may write it. More than 256 names is refused 413.

get.summary: Lists the external MCP servers the caller's org has registered.
get.description:
Lists the external MCP servers the caller's org has registered.
Each record carries the URL and the name of the header its credential is
injected into; the credential VALUE lives only in KMS and is never returned,
so hasSecret is the whole of what this surface says about it. Each also says
whether its tools could be listed — status, a reason when they could not, and
how many there are — so a server that contributes nothing says why.

The whole URL is answered to an admin of the org or a SuperAdmin, who register
servers. A member is answered its scheme and host: which server it is, and not
a path or query an admin may have put a key in.

post.summary: Gives the caller's org one more external MCP server, so its tools join the org's tool plane and the fleet's MCP server.
post.description:
Gives the caller's org one more external MCP server, so its tools
join the org's tool plane and the fleet's MCP server. It is the ONE way an org
gains a server, whether it typed the URL in or enabled a catalog listing: both
write the SAME record, and `source` says which it was. A second registration
path would be a second place for a server to exist, and then a second place to
forget to check the credential.

The credential VALUE is sealed in KMS under a per-org ref; the row keeps only
the URL, the header name to inject it into, and a has-secret flag — so a secret
with no KMS configured is refused 503 rather than stored in the clear. The URL
is SSRF-validated here and re-checked by the dialer at connect time, which is
the DNS-rebinding defense.

Enabling a listing the org already enabled REVISES that server rather than
adding a near-duplicate beside it, so a retried enable is the same one server.
Answers 201 with the stored record.

A server and the tools of it the org activates are carried into every agent run
in the org, so registering one — or revising one, credential included — takes
an admin of the org or a SuperAdmin; a member is refused 403. The registration
is on the org's audit trail before it is made, and one the trail cannot record
is refused 503.

delete.summary: Deregisters one of the caller org's external MCP servers, so its tools leave the registry.
delete.description:
Deregisters one of the caller org's external MCP servers, so its
tools leave the registry. Scoped to the caller's org, so an id belonging to
another tenant is a 404 and not a delete. Answers 204 with no body; a server
this org does not have is 404. Like registering one it takes an admin of the
org or a SuperAdmin, and is on the org's audit trail before it is made.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the server to deregister, from the path.

get.summary: Reports what this deployment actually mounted: every subsystem the composition root declared and whether it is switched on.
get.description:
Reports what this deployment actually mounted: every subsystem the
composition root declared and whether it is switched on. A plugin here is
MOUNTED CODE that extends the deployment's own surface — not a tool an agent
calls — so this is an inventory and not a tool source. It is read off the same
boot snapshot every traced request resolves its subsystem label against, so it
cannot drift from what is serving. Enabled-only by default, because a caller
asking what this deployment can do wants what is running; ?all=true adds the
configured-but-off ones.

parameters.name: all
parameters.description:
All includes the configured-but-disabled subsystems too, but only when it is
exactly the string "true". Otherwise only the running ones are reported.

get.summary: Lists the plugins the caller's org BUILT, newest first, each with the TypeScript as authored.
get.description:
Lists the plugins the caller's org BUILT, newest first,
each with the TypeScript as authored. That is a different set with a different
lifecycle from GET /v1/tool/plugins, which reports the subsystems this deployment
mounted. The bundled CommonJS the runtime executes is never included, and
neither is any credential — a plugin names the connectors provider it needs and
reads the credential from ctx.auth at run time.

delete.summary: Removes one of the caller org's built plugins, so the runtime can no longer load it.
delete.description:
Removes one of the caller org's built plugins, so the
runtime can no longer load it. Scoped to the caller's org, so an id belonging
to another tenant answers 404 and is not deleted.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the plugin to remove, from the path.

post.summary: Builds and stores one plugin for the caller's org.
post.description:
Builds and stores one plugin for the caller's org. The 201 carries
the bundle's size, whether a model wrote the source, and the plugin as stored.

Post `source` to build TypeScript as-is, or `spec` — an OpenAPI document or
plain prose describing the endpoints — to have one generated; the generated
source comes back in the answer, so a caller reads what will run before it
runs. Exactly one of the two, and `name` must be one lowercase path segment;
both or neither is 400.

COMPILING IS THE GATE. The source goes through the same pipeline the committed
connectors do — esbuild to one CommonJS program, then compiled in the goja
runtime that will actually execute it — and anything that fails is rejected and
NEVER stored. So a plugin in the store is one this deployment has already
loaded once, not one a model claimed was fine. A failed build answers 422
carrying the diagnostics a caller needs to fix it: the bundler's error
(`detail`), the source that failed, and whether the model wrote it.

CREDENTIALS ARE NOT PART OF A PLUGIN. A plugin names the connectors `provider`
it needs and reads that credential from `ctx.auth` at run time, under KMS
custody. Source that carries something key-shaped is REFUSED rather than
silently persisted — a scrubbed key looks like it worked.

get.summary: Lists the skills the caller's org can reach — the brand's embedded catalogue plus the org's own authored ones — with each one's activation flag.
get.description:
Lists the skills the caller's org can reach — the brand's embedded
catalogue plus the org's own authored ones — with each one's activation flag.
A skill is discovery and activation metadata attached to an agent, never called
directly, so every entry here is non-dispatchable. It is GET /v1/tool narrowed
to one source, not a second store: a name a caller sees here is the same entry,
with the same activation state, that discovery reports.

parameters.name: activated
parameters.description:
Activated keeps only the tools activated for the caller's org and project,
and only when it is exactly the string "true".

post.summary: Adds or revises one of the caller org's own skills, and answers 201 with the stored record.
post.description:
Adds or revises one of the caller org's own skills, and answers 201
with the stored record. The id is derived from the name, so writing the same
name again REVISES that skill rather than accumulating near-duplicates that
would then collide in the registry. An org's skills are private to it by
construction — they live in a different store from the brand's embedded
catalogue and have no path into the public gallery — and a brand skill always
wins a name collision against an org's.

An activated skill is carried into every agent run in the org, so writing one
takes an admin of the org or a SuperAdmin; a member is refused 403. The write is
on the org's audit trail before it is made, and one the trail cannot record is
refused 503.

get.summary: Lists the caller org's OWN skills with their SKILL.md bodies.
get.description:
Lists the caller org's OWN skills with their SKILL.md
bodies. GET /v1/tool/skills is the registry view — the brand's catalogue plus this
org's, with activation flags and no bodies; this is the EDITABLE set, so it
carries the content that view omits and nothing the org did not write.

delete.summary: Removes one of the caller org's authored skills.
delete.description:
Removes one of the caller org's authored skills. Scoped to the
caller's org, so an id belonging to another tenant is never reached. Removing
what is not there is not an error — the caller's intent is "gone", and it is.
Like writing one it takes an admin of the org or a SuperAdmin, and is on the
org's audit trail before it is made.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the skill to remove, from the path. It is the skill's name.

code.description: A stable token a client can branch on, when the refusal names one.

detail.description: What was refused, for a person to read.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is when the plugin was last built, Unix seconds.

id.description: ID is the plugin's id within the org, and the id a delete addresses.

name.description: Name is the plugin's name: one lowercase path segment, the id it runs by.

org.description: Org is the org that built the plugin — the validated caller's.

provider.description:
Provider is the connectors provider whose credential this plugin uses at
run time. Absent for a plugin that needs none. The credential itself is
never here — it stays under KMS custody in the connectors plane.

source.description: Source is the TypeScript as authored (or as generated from a spec).

excess.description: Excess are servers left out, by id, because a run carries only so many.

muted.description:
Muted are the names the run's person took out of their own runs — a
skill, a server's tool, or a server by its id. None of them is above.

omitted.description: Omitted are activated skills left out because a run carries only so many.

servers.description:
Servers are the MCP servers an admin registered and activated tools of, at
most KitServers of them.

skills.description: Skills are the documents of the skills an admin activated, by name.

description.description: Description is the publisher's one-line summary.

featured.description: Featured puts the listing on the front of the shelf. Curation.

hidden.description:
Hidden keeps the listing out of the org-visible catalog. Curation: a sync
never changes it. Only a SuperAdmin sets it, and only a SuperAdmin sees a
hidden entry listed.

id.description:
ID addresses the listing in a URL. It is the reverse-DNS NAME with its one
slash written as an underscore — reversible, because a namespace never
contains an underscore — so the id is readable and stable rather than a
hash that means nothing to whoever reads a link.

logo.description:
Logo is the brand mark to render for the listing — the publisher's icon when
the entry carries one, or the one an admin set. Curation.

name.description: Name is the publisher's reverse-DNS name, e.g. "com.stripe/mcp".

official.description:
Official is whether this is the vendor's OWN server rather than someone
else's copy of it. Derived on every sync (see isOfficial) until a
SuperAdmin sets it explicitly, after which the admin's answer stands.

packages.description:
Packages are the runnable package forms — npm, pypi, oci — each with the
runtime that launches it and the transport it then speaks.

registry.description: Registry is the upstream this row was synced from.

remotes.description: Remotes are the hosted endpoints the publisher serves the server at.

repo.description: Repo is the source repository URL, when the entry names one.

site.description: Site is the project's homepage, when the entry names one.

synced.description: Synced is when this row was last confirmed against upstream, Unix seconds.

title.description: Title is the human-readable display name, when the entry carries one.

transports.description:
Transports are the distinct transports this server can be reached over,
sorted: some of "stdio", "streamable-http", "sse". A listing with
"streamable-http" is one an org can enable here and now; a listing that is
only "stdio" needs a process to run it.

vendor.description: Vendor is the namespace half of Name — the publisher, e.g. "com.stripe".

version.description: Version is the published version of this listing.

identifier.description: Identifier is the package name or download URL.

registry.description: Registry is where the package is fetched from: npm, pypi, oci, nuget, mcpb.

runtime.description: Runtime is the publisher's hint for what launches it: npx, uvx, docker.

transport.description: Transport is what the launched process speaks: usually "stdio".

version.description: Version is the exact published package version.

admitted.description:
Admitted is whether an admin of the org, or a SuperAdmin, registered the
server. Only an admitted server is carried into the org's agent runs: a
server registered before registering one took an admin is not, until an
admin registers it again.

authHeader.description:
AuthHeader is the request header the KMS-held credential is injected into,
e.g. "Authorization". Absent when the server needs no credential.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is when the server was registered, Unix seconds.

hasSecret.description:
HasSecret is whether a credential is sealed in KMS for this server. The
VALUE is never returned by any route.

id.description:
ID is the server's id within the org. It also PREFIXES every tool name the
server contributes, which is what keeps two servers' "search" apart.

listing.description:
Listing is the catalog entry this server was enabled from, when it was.
Empty means the org typed the URL in itself.

name.description: Name is the org's label for the server.

org.description: Org is the org that registered the server — the validated caller's.

reason.description:
Reason says why a server that is not "ok" is not, in words any member may
be shown: never the server's address.

source.description:
Source is where the registration came from: "catalog" when it was enabled
off the shelf, "org" when the org registered the URL itself. It is DERIVED
from Listing rather than stored, because two columns for one fact is two
chances to disagree.

status.description:
Status is whether the server's tools could be listed when the org's
servers were read: "ok", "unreachable", "refused" or "error". Only the
listing answers it; a registration does not.

tools.description: Tools is how many tools the server listed, when it listed them.

url.description:
URL is the server's JSON-RPC endpoint. Always a public http(s) host: the
registration boundary and the dialer both refuse anything else.

amount.description:
Amount is what ONE call costs, EXACTLY: an 18-decimal USD value, so a
per-call price of $0.0025 is $0.0025 and not a cent-floored zero. Cents
cannot hold a per-token price, and a tool plane is where per-token prices
live.

currency.description: Currency is the ISO 4217 code, e.g. "USD". Empty means USD.

recipient.description: Recipient is the payout wallet ref the marketplace seller is paid at.

name.description:
Name is the server's id in the org, which also prefixes its tools on the
tool plane, and names it to ToolsRelay.

tools.description:
Tools are the tools of it an admin activated, each by the server's own
name for it: all a run's harness may call of it.

admitted.description:
Admitted is whether an admin of the org, or a SuperAdmin, wrote this
content. Only admitted content is carried into the org's agent runs. A
push writes content nobody administering the org attested, and a skill
written before writing one took an admin says no until an admin writes it
again.

content.description: Content is the SKILL.md body, markdown.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is when the skill was last written, Unix seconds.

description.description: Description is the one-line summary discovery shows for the skill.

id.description:
ID is the skill's id within the org. It is DERIVED from Name, so writing
the same name again revises that skill rather than adding another.

name.description: Name is the skill's name: one lowercase path segment (a-z0-9, _ or -).

org.description:
Org is the org that authored the skill — the validated caller's, never a
value the body supplied.

source.description:
Source is the repository the skill was read from, "<project>/<name>" or
"<name>"; empty for a skill written through the API. A push replaces every
skill of its source at once, so a skill leaves when its file does.

content.description: Content is the skill's SKILL.md, verbatim.

name.description:
Name is the skill's bare name, which is also the directory its SKILL.md
is written into.

activated.description:
Activated is filled by the registry from the activation store for the
requesting (org,project); providers leave it zero. An unactivated tool is
discoverable but refused 403 at dispatch.

description.description: Description is the prose a model reads to decide whether to call the tool.

dispatchable.description:
Dispatchable is whether the tool can be CALLED. False for a listing-only
entry: a skill is activated and attached to an agent, never called.

inputSchema.description:
Schema is the JSON Schema of the call arguments — the MCP inputSchema.
Absent for a tool that takes none.

name.description:
Name is the tool's id in the flat, fleet-wide tool namespace — the value a
tools/call passes. Unique across sources: a collision is resolved by source
precedence before the caller ever sees it.

price.description:
Price is what a call costs and who is paid, absent for a free tool.
Enforcement is the x402 settlement client; this is the declaration.

source.description:
Source is where the tool comes from: connector, function, zap-service,
agent, skill or mcp.

activate.description: Activate switches these tool names on for the caller's org and project.

deactivate.description: Deactivate switches these tool names off.

enabled.description: Enabled is every tool name activated for the caller's org and project.

plugins.description:
Plugins is every plugin this org built, newest first, each carrying the
TypeScript as authored. The bundled artifact is never rendered.

skills.description: Skills is every skill this org authored, each with its SKILL.md content.

bytes.description: Bytes is the size of the bundled CommonJS the runtime will execute.

generated.description:
Generated is whether a model wrote the source from a spec, rather than the
caller posting the source itself.

plugin.description: Plugin is the plugin as stored, with its derived id and build time.

name.description:
Name is the plugin's name: one lowercase path segment (a-z0-9, _ or -),
and the id the runtime loads it by.

provider.description:
Provider is the connectors provider whose credential the plugin reads at
run time. Empty for a plugin that needs none.

source.description: Source is TypeScript to build as-is. Exactly one of Source or Spec.

spec.description:
Spec is API documentation — an OpenAPI document, or prose describing the
endpoints — that the generator turns into Source. The generated source is
returned in the response, so a caller can read what will run before it runs.

authHeader.description:
AuthHeader is the request header the credential is injected into, e.g.
"Authorization". Empty means the server needs no credential.

listing.description:
Listing enables a CATALOG entry instead — the id from GET /v1/tool/catalog.
The endpoint is the listing's own streamable-http remote, so a listing that
only ships a stdio package is refused: there is nothing to reach yet.

name.description:
Name labels the server for the org. Required with URL; with Listing it
defaults to the listing's own title.

secret.description:
Secret is the credential VALUE. It is sealed into KMS under a per-org ref
and never stored in SQLite, never listed, and never returned.

url.description:
URL is the server's JSON-RPC endpoint. It must be an http(s) URL naming a
PUBLIC host: loopback, link-local, private and cloud-metadata addresses are
refused here and again when the dialer connects. A URL carrying a credential
(user:password@) is refused: the credential is the secret.

featured.description: Featured puts the listing on the front of the shelf, or takes it off.

hidden.description: Hidden takes the listing off the org-visible shelf, or puts it back.

id.description: ID is the listing to curate, from the path.

logo.description:
Logo is the brand mark to render, an https URL. Empty clears ours and lets
the next sync adopt the publisher's own icon again.

official.description:
Official overrides the derivation: setting it makes this answer FINAL, so
no later sync re-derives over it. That is the difference between a default
and a decision — the derivation can only tell that a domain-verified
publisher serves the endpoint, not that the product is theirs.

activated.description:
Activated reports whether the candidate is switched on for the caller's
org and project after processing autoActivate.

description.description: Description summarizes what the skill or tool does.

name.description:
Name is the tool or skill identifier as reported by GET /v1/tool (for
example "skill_dev", "skill_ui", or "github_create_issue").

probability.description:
Probability is how likely the candidate fits the prompt, in [0, 1];
0.8 or more means it clearly does.

source.description:
Source names the provider that owns the entry: skill, mcp, connector,
function, agent or zap-service.

autoActivate.description:
AutoActivate switches on the recommended skills and tools that the caller
is permitted to activate for the current org and project scope.

maxSkills.description: MaxSkills bounds how many skills are returned (default 6, max 16).

maxTools.description: MaxTools bounds how many callable tools are returned (default 8, max 32).

prompt.description:
Prompt is the user message, task description, or conversation turn to
evaluate against the organization's available skills and tools.

threshold.description:
Threshold is the minimum calibrated probability (0 to 1, default 0.55) a
skill or tool must score to be recommended.

activated.description:
Activated lists the tool and skill names that were newly switched on by
this call when autoActivate was set.

decisionId.description:
DecisionID is the identifier of the decision (POST /v1/decisions) the
candidates were ranked by, when a decision model ranked them; absent
from rank-1.

model.description: Model names what ranked the candidates ("rank-1").

skills.description:
Skills lists the recommended skills (skill_<name>), ordered from highest
to lowest probability.

tools.description:
Tools lists the recommended callable tools, ordered from highest to
lowest probability.

catalog.description: Catalog is this page of listings, featured first, then by name.

limit.description:
Limit is the page size that was actually applied — the default or the clamp,
when the request asked for neither or for too much.

offset.description:
Offset is where this page started, so a caller pages from what the server
did rather than from what it asked for.

total.description:
Total is how many listings the filter matched, which is more than this page
holds whenever there is a next one.

added.description: Added is how many listings the catalog did not have before.

registry.description: Registry is the upstream this pass read.

total.description: Total is how many listings the catalog holds now.

updated.description: Updated is how many the publisher has changed since we last looked.

servers.description:
Servers is every external MCP server this org has registered. No secret
VALUE is ever included — only whether one is set.

mute.description:
Mute takes these out of the caller's runs: a skill (skill_<name>), a
server's tool (<server>_<tool>) or a whole server (<server>), each one the
org's kit carries.

unmute.description: Unmute gives these back, as far as the org's kit carries them.

deleted.description: Deleted is the plugin id that is now gone.

enabled.description: Enabled is whether this subsystem is switched on in this deployment.

name.description: Name is the subsystem's name, the same label a traced request resolves to.

prefixes.description: Prefixes are the URL prefixes this subsystem serves.

plugins.description:
Plugins is every subsystem the composition root declared, filtered to the
enabled ones unless all=true.

deleted.description: Deleted is the skill id that is now gone.

content.description: Content is the SKILL.md body. Required, at most 256 KiB.

description.description: Description is the one-line summary discovery shows for the skill.

name.description:
Name is the skill's id within the org: one lowercase path segment
(a-z0-9, _ or -). Writing an existing name REVISES that skill.

skill.description: Skill is the skill as stored, with its derived id and creation time.

source.description: Source is the source these tools came from.

tools.description: Tools is the caller's tools from that source. Never null.

arguments.description:
Arguments is the tool's own input object, passed through verbatim to
whichever source owns it.

name.description: Name is the tool to run, exactly as GET /v1/tool reports it.

incomplete.description:
Incomplete names the sources that did not answer this listing, and
"activation" when the activation store could not be read. Tools from a named
source are absent, not nonexistent, and with "activation" every activated flag
reads false. Omitted when every source answered.

tools.description:
Tools is every tool the caller may see, deduplicated by name with source
precedence applied.

name.description: Name is the tool that ran.

result.description:
Result is the tool's own output, verbatim — its shape is the tool's, not
this plane's.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
